s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive systemic illness with generalized weakness, weight loss, and multi-organ involvement
key_facts: Six months of progressive generalized weakness
Noncompliant with lisinopril for over three years
Dullness to percussion and decreased breath sounds at the left lung base
Blood urea nitrogen 60 mg/dL, creatinine 1.69 mg/dL
Chest radiography showed bilateral pleural effusions
High titers of ANA, anti–double-stranded DNA, and anti–Smith antibodies
Urinalysis showed pH 5, 16 WBCs and 27 RBCs per high-power field

raw.syndrome_frame: Progressive systemic illness with generalized weakness, weight loss, and multi-organ involvement
key_facts: Six months of progressive generalized weakness
Noncompliant with lisinopril for over three years
Dullness to percussion and decreased breath sounds at the left lung base
Blood urea nitrogen 60 mg/dL, creatinine 1.69 mg/dL
Chest radiography showed bilateral pleural effusions
High titers of ANA, anti–double-stranded DNA, and anti–Smith antibodies
Urinalysis showed pH 5, 16 WBCs and 27 RBCs per high-power field

shortlist.label: Systemic lupus erythematosus
shortlist.why_kept: High titers of ANA, anti–double-stranded DNA, and anti–Smith antibodies, with low complement C3 levels, and multi-organ involvement

shortlist.label: Sarcoidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Non-tender lymphadenopathy, bilateral pleural effusions, and multi-organ involvement

shortlist.label: Wegener's granulomatosis
shortlist.why_kept: Renal involvement with proteinuria and hematuria, and respiratory symptoms with pleural effusions

shortlist.label: Lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Generalized weakness, weight loss, and lymphadenopathy

shortlist.label: Castleman disease
shortlist.why_kept: Lymphadenopathy, multi-organ involvement, and systemic symptoms

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with progressive generalized weakness, weight loss, dyspnea, mucosal pallor, lymphadenopathy, and pleural effusions, along with laboratory findings of anemia, leukopenia, and elevated inflammatory markers, is consistent with a systemic autoimmune disease. The presence of high titers of ANA, anti-double-stranded DNA, and anti-Smith antibodies, as well as low complement C3 levels, strongly supports the diagnosis of systemic lupus erythematosus.

rejected.label: Sarcoidosis
rejected.why: While sarcoidosis can present with lymphadenopathy and pleural effusions, the absence of granulomas on biopsy and the presence of specific autoantibodies make it less likely.

rejected.label: Wegener's granulomatosis
rejected.why: The lack of granulomatous inflammation and the presence of anti-Smith antibodies make this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Lymphoma
rejected.why: The negative lymph node biopsy and the presence of specific autoantibodies make lymphoma an unlikely diagnosis.

rejected.label: Castleman disease
rejected.why: While Castleman disease can present with lymphadenopathy and systemic symptoms, the presence of specific autoantibodies and the lack of characteristic histopathological findings make it less likely.
